#!/bin/sh

#FLUX -J gfs_wafs_blending
#FLUX --workdir=/gpfs/hps/ptmp/Yali.Mao
#FLUX --output=/gpfs/hps/ptmp/Yali.Mao/gfs_wafs_blending.o{{id}}
#FLUX --error=/gpfs/hps/ptmp/Yali.Mao/gfs_wafs_blending.o{{id}}
#FLUX -p debug
#FLUX -t 00:30:00
#FLUX -A GFS-T2O
#FLUX --mem-per-cpu=500M
# From -R '1*{select[craylinux && !vnode]} + 1*{select[craylinux && vnode]span[ptile=24] cu[type=cabinet]}'
#FLUX -N 1
#FLUX -n 24
#FLUX --ntasks-per-node=24

# The following LSF directives were not translated:
# #BSUB -extsched 'CRAYLINUX[]': This is a system-specific LSF scheduling hint without a direct Flux equivalent.
# #BSUB -R '...select[craylinux]...cu[type=cabinet]': Resource selection constraints are system-specific and cannot be translated without knowing the target system's Flux configuration. The job will run on any available resources in the specified queue, which may have different performance characteristics.

############################################
# Loading module
############################################
. $MODULESHOME/init/ksh
module load PrgEnv-intel ESMF-intel-haswell/3_1_0rp5 cfp-intel-sandybridge iobuf craype-hugepages2M craype-haswell
#module load cfp-intel-sandybridge/1.1.0
module use /gpfs/hps/nco/ops/nwprod/modulefiles
module load prod_envir/1.1.0
module load prod_util/1.0.4
module load grib_util/1.0.3


set -xa

export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export KMP_AFFINITY=disabled
export OMP_STACKSIZE=1024m
export MP_LABELIO=yes
export MP_STDOUTMODE=ordered 

####export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
####export MP_MPILIB=mpich2
####export MP_EUILIB=us
####export MP_LABELIO=yes
####export MP_COMPILER=intel

############################################
# required exports!
############################################
### envir: prod/dev/para/bkup/ges/test bkup2/ges2/para2/prod2/prd_p6
export envir=para

export cyc=${cyc:-00}

# gfs_wafs_blending for blending icing turbulence of US and UK
export job=gfs_wafs_blending_${cyc}

############################################
# set NET RUN
############################################
### NET: gfs/para/parallel-test/nam/rap/ dump/ens/nawips/nesdis/
export NET=gfs
export RUN=gfs


############################################
# Specify versions
############################################
export gfs_ver=v4.0.0


############################################
# user defined
############################################
export pid=${pid:-$$}
export jobid=${job}.${pid}

#needs to be the current date to make sure comparison is good at $PCOM
#export PDY=`$NDATE -24 | cut -c 1-8`
export PDY=`cut -c 7-14 $COMROOT/date/t00z`
export PDY=20161101

USER=`whoami`

############################################
# SENDCOM=YES--Copy output file to /com
# SENDECF=YES--Allow to talk back to ECF
# SENDDBN=YES--Alert output file to TOC
# KEEPDATA=NO--Remove temporary working
############################################
export SENDCOM=YES
export SENDDBN=NO
export SENDDBN_NTC=NO
export KEEPDATA=YES
 
############################################
# Define ROOT directories
############################################
echo $COMROOT
#export NWROOTp1=/nwprod
export PCOMROOT=/gpfs/hps/ptmp/${USER}/pcom
#export PCOMROOT=/gpfs/gp1/ptmp/Yali.Mao
export NWROOT=/gpfs/hps/emc/global/noscrub/Yali.Mao/project
export DATAROOT=/gpfs/hps/ptmp/${USER}
# for UK data
if [[ `hostname` =~ "^l" ]] ; then ! LUNA/TIDE
  export DCOMROOT=/gpfs/tp1/nco/ops/dcom
else                               ! SURGE/GYRE
  export DCOMROOT=/gpfs/gp1/nco/ops/dcom
fi
# For canned data:
export DCOMROOT=/gpfs/hps/emc/global/noscrub/Yali.Mao/datainput/dcom

############################################
# Define DATA PCOM, COMOUT and COMIN
############################################
export DATA=${DATA:-${DATAROOT}/${jobid}}
export PCOM=${PCOM:-$PCOMROOT/wafs}
export COMOUT=/gpfs/hps/ptmp/${USER}/gfs_wafs_blending.$PDY

export COMINus=$PCOM
#export COMINus=/gpfs/gp2/nco/ops/pcom/prod/wafs
export COMINuk=${COMINuk:-$DCOMROOT/us007003/$PDY/wgrbbul/ukmet_wafs}

export jlogfile=/$DATA/jlogfile.${jobid}

################################
# Set up the HOME directory
################################
export HOMEgfs=${HOMEgfs:-${NWROOT}/wafs_cray.${gfs_ver}}


############################################
# run the job
#############################################
export SHOUR=06
export EHOUR=36
export FHINC=03

sh $HOMEgfs/jobs/JGFS_WAFS_BLENDING

exit

#############################################
# compare the output (optional)
#############################################
if [ $USER = 'Yali.Mao' ] ; then

  # the standard data to be compared to
  stdout=/com/${NET}/$envir/${RUN}.${PDY}
  if [ $envir = prod ]; then
    stdpcom=/pcom/wafs
  else
    stdpcom=/pcom/${envir}/wafs
  fi

  ffhr=$SHOUR

  while test $ffhr -le $EHOUR ; do

    cmp $COMOUT/WAFS_blended_${PDY}${cyc}f${ffhr}.grib2 $stdout/WAFS_blended_${PDY}${cyc}f${ffhr}.grib2

    # $PCOM data on develop machine may be out of date, so skip the comparison
    continue

    cmp $PCOM/grib2.t${cyc}z.WAFS_blended_f${ffhr} $stdpcom/grib2.t${cyc}z.WAFS_blended_f${ffhr}

    ffhr=`expr $ffhr + $FHINC`
    if test $ffhr -lt 10
    then
      ffhr=0${ffhr}
    fi

  done

fi
exit

reasons: Invalid job ID placeholder '{{id}}' used in --output and --error directives. The correct format for Flux is '{id}' or '{jobid}'.
issues: The script contains unreachable code. An `exit` command is placed immediately after the main job execution call (`sh $HOMEgfs/jobs/JGFS_WAFS_BLENDING`), which prevents the subsequent 'compare the output' block from ever running.

The shebang is `#!/bin/sh`, but the script uses ksh/bash specific syntax (e.g., `. $MODULESHOME/init/ksh`, `[[ ... ]]`). The shebang should be changed to `#!/bin/ksh` or `#!/bin/bash` for consistency and correctness.

The script has a hardcoded date `export PDY=20161101`, which overrides a previous command intended to set it dynamically. This is likely intended for a test but is a potential source of error in production.

The variable `$COMROOT` is used to define `PDY` before it is defined within the script itself. This implies that `$COMROOT` must be inherited from the submission environment, which can make the script less reliable.
The final comparison block is hardcoded to run only for the user 'Yali.Mao', which reduces the script's portability.
